newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Consortium bids 90 Sfr for Ciba rights.
newsitem.headline: Consortium bids 90 Sfr for Ciba rights.

text.p: A bank consortium said it would bid 90 Swiss francs per subscription right for shares in Ciba Specialty Holding Inc, which is being spun off from Novartis.
Rights closed up 2.35 francs today at 101.50, valuing Ciba shares at 111.50 given the 10-franc subscription price.
The bank consortium will acquire rights to get shares it will then place in a global offering. UBS and Credit Suisse First Boston are global coordinators for the offering.

Rights will be tendered to the consortium tomorrow. Rights end trading at noon (1100 GMT) on March 12. The global offer price and allotment will be announced on March 13, the same day 72.1 million Ciba SC shares are listed.
UBS and CSFB said last week shares may be priced above the range of 72 to 86 Swiss francs per share originally announced for the global offering given higher prices for the rights.
The consortium last month set a minimum price of 64 Swiss francs it would pay for rights in Ciba, which is being spun off via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders.
The global offering will have at least 300 million Swiss francs worth of stock. It was for this offer that the indicated range of 72 to 86 francs was set last month.
The rights, which began trading on February 26, have been holding well above this price amid strong demand.

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion Swiss francs from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's market leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.
